I am always right.|[[TX-20/Legends|TX-20]] and [[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor]] on [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]]|audio=IAmAlwaysRight-IoR.flac|<ref name="Innocents of Ryloth">{{TCW|Innocents of Ryloth}}</ref>}}
The '''T-series tactical droid''', formerly known as the '''CDE-T unit'''<ref name="TEGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> or '''standard tactical droid''', was a model of [[Tactical droid/Legends|tactical droid]] serving the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] (CIS) during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The [[Super tactical droid/Legends|super tactical droid]] was later created as an upgraded tactical droid model.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|That droid exaggerates.|Wat Tambor, to Dooku, about TA-175|<ref name="Innocents of Ryloth" />}}
[[File:TacticalDroid-GaW.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A tactical droid directs a B1 battle droid's operation of a [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]]]]
The T-series [[Tactical droid/Legends|tactical droid]] was more intelligent than standard battle droids and was deployed to command Separatist troops where organic leadership was not available. They had advanced combat-analysis software and were very intelligent.<ref name="GAW" /> They were designed with advanced cognitive modules that processed vast quantities of data rapidly, and would constantly run simulations of imminent combat, calculating odds to develop strategies.<ref name="TEGTW" />

Their bodies were approximately the same size as a [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 super battle droid]], but were boxier than their combat-designed compatriots. In addition, their voices lacked any inflection, and instead spoke in a flat, droning monotone. Tactical droids were observed to be impatient, arrogant, pushy, and demanding.<ref name="TEGTW" /> They believed themselves superior to other droids, as evidenced by their poor treatment of and insults to battle droids, such as during the battles of [[Quell/Legends|Quell]] and [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]]. They often issued conflicting orders due to their sense of superiority.<ref name="GAW" /> When pushed, tactical droids would even order the destruction of their own allies if they got in the way, as seen at the [[Sky Battle of Quell]].<ref name="Jedi Crash">{{TCW|Jedi Crash}}</ref> Some of these droids were in charge of entire fleets and land forces. Most Separatist leaders allowed tactical droids greater autonomy over their forces.<ref name="TEGTW" />

Tactical droids were not as homogeneous as other [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droid]] models. The personalities and voices between units varied slightly, making no two units identical. Tactical droids bore colorful paint schemes, each of which was unique as well.

==History==
{{Quote|The general's description of your tactics have been one hundred percent accurate today. Very impressive, even by ''my'' standards.|TV-94, on General Grievous' description of Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="Grievous Intrigue">{{TCW|Grievous Intrigue}}</ref>}}
During the first weeks of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], a T-series tactical droid with feminine programming identified as [[Blue-Tark/Legends|Blue-Tark]] was in service to the Separatist-aligned genetic terrorist [[Zeta Magnus]], operating under Magnus' command within his personal dominion of the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] known as the [[Dark Worlds]].<ref name="SkyeWalkers">''[[SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story]]''</ref> She would be assigned by Magnus to oversee his conquest of the remote planet [[Skye/Legends|Skye]] under the command of a [[Zeta Magnus (clone)|clone of Magnus]], though she would be forced to flee off-planet when a [[Battle of Skye|revolt]] from the native [[S'kytri]] species instigated by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] destroyed the clone and the bulk of its forces. Retreating to the Dark Worlds, Blue-Tark reported the incident to Zeta Magnus directly. 

At least three tactical droids were used in the staging of the [[Battle of Christophsis/Legends|Battle of Christophsis]]. [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Trench/Legends|Trench]] used a tactical droid named [[TI-99/Legends|TI-99]] aboard his [[Invincible/Legends|command ship]].<ref name="Cat and Mouse">{{TCW|Cat and Mouse}}</ref> One such droid, [[TJ-55/Legends|TJ-55]], had its head stolen to discover how the CIS knew the Republic's strategies, and a clone traitor was later revealed. [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] later dispatched [[Unidentified T-series tactical droid (Christophsis)/Legends|another tactical droid]] to give orders to [[General/Legends|General]] [[Whorm Loathsom/Legends|Whorm Loathsom]] while she left to continue [[Dooku/Legends|her master's]] plan.<ref name="Hidden Enemy">{{TCW|The Hidden Enemy}}</ref>

Another such droid, named [[TX-20/Legends|TX-20]], was stationed on [[Count/Legends|Count]] Dooku's command ship during the events of the [[Battle of Ryloth/Legends|Battle of Ryloth]], where he sent a message to [[Lott Dod/Legends|Lott Dod]] to go to [[Toydaria/Legends|Toydaria]].<ref name="Supply Lines">{{TCW|Supply Lines}}</ref>

[[File:STAPs_BSV.jpg|thumb|200px|A tactical droid on Naboo with three battle droids]]
Later during the war, [[Clone Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Bly/Legends|Bly]] and [[Jedi General/Legends|General]] [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]] encountered a [[Unidentified T-series tactical droid (Aayla Secura's ambush)|tactical droid]] on one of [[Battle for the Galactic Republic information bunker|their missions]]. They planned on using the droid's severed head to search for [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] secrets.<ref name="Headgames">''[[The Clone Wars: Headgames]]''</ref> Sometime later, during the [[Sky Battle of Quell]], another tactical droid, [[TF-1726/Legends|TF-1726]], was used to dispatch orders on board a [[Munificent-class star frigate/Legends|''Munificent''-class star frigate]].<ref name="Jedi Crash" />

On Naboo, a [[Unidentified T-series tactical droid|tactical droid]] was used to carry out orders while [[Doctor/Legends|Dr.]] [[Nuvo Vindi/Legends|Nuvo Vindi]] was planning to release the [[Blue Shadow Virus/Legends|Blue Shadow Virus]] back into the galaxy. The droid used a [[Flitknot speeder/Legends|Flitknot speeder]] to scope out the area with three [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|STAP]]-mounted [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-series battle droids]]. His speeder was destroyed, and the droids' remains were taken back to [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] so they could be scanned. This eventually led to the discovery of [[Trade Federation laboratory/Legends|Vindi's laboratory]].<ref name="Blue Shadow Virus (episode)">{{TCW|Blue Shadow Virus (episode)}}</ref>

TX-20 also led droids during the Battle of Ryloth, under the watchful eye of [[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor]], and was in charge of the [[Proton cannon/Legends|proton cannons]] there.<ref name="Innocents of Ryloth" /> TX-20 took the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]] of [[Nabat/Legends|Nabat]] hostage and used them as a "living shield" for the cannons. TX-20 also employed [[Gutkurr/Legends|gutkurrs]] to attack the Republic forces. However, after [[High Jedi General/Legends|General]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] freed the Twi'lek prisoners, the former hostages destroyed the unit.

Another such droid, [[TA-175/Legends|TA-175]], served to command the operations of the Separatist fortress at the capital city of [[Lessu City/Legends|Lessu]] on Ryloth. This unit was very strict in obeying orders and maintaining schedules, to the point where he ordered the departure of the evacuation shuttle from the planet, abandoning Wat Tambor, who selfishly refused to leave until the delayed [[Multi-Troop Transport/Legends|MTTs]] carrying the last of the spoils arrived. The droid disobeyed Tambor's commands in doing so, rigidly acknowledging Count Dooku's superiority in the situation.<ref name="Liberty on Ryloth">{{TCW|Liberty on Ryloth}}</ref>

During the [[Battle of Juma 9]], a tactical droid relayed orders to battle droids on the station. He was cut down by [[Luminara Unduli/Legends|Luminara Unduli]] and [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]]. Later, [[Unidentified T-series tactical droid (Mustafar)|two more droids]] were used during a battle on Mustafar.

[[File:Doctor_tactical_droid.png|thumb|left|180px|Doctor, a modified tactical droid]]
A [[Doctor (tactical droid)|heavily modified tactical droid]] served [[Magistrate/Legends|Magistrate]] [[Passel Argente/Legends|Passel Argente]]. The droid later participated in and was destroyed during the [[battle of Ukio]].

[[TX-21/Legends|TX-21]] served [[Archduke/Legends|Archduke]] [[Poggle the Lesser/Legends|Poggle the Lesser]] on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] at the time of the [[Second Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Second Battle of Geonosis]]. It encountered [[Jedi Commander/Legends|Jedi Commanders]] [[Barriss Offee/Legends|Barriss Offee]] and [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] in the control center of a new [[Droid factory|droid foundry]]. Tano threw an explosive device at the droid, and it attached itself to the [[Separatist super-tank prototype/Legends|super tank]] TX-21 was standing beside. The tactical droid laughed, stating that the super tank could not be damaged by such a device. He was correct; though there was no damage to the tank, TX-21 was destroyed by the explosion.<ref name="Weapons Factory">{{TCW|Weapons Factory}}</ref>

A tactical droid was used by the CIS during their occupation of [[Tirahnn/Legends|Tirahnn]], to work in the command center of a planetary [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]] that was located in the world's [[Tirahnn (city)|capital city]].<ref name="GAW" /> Another tactical droid, [[TV-94/Legends|TV-94]], served as the personal assistant to General [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] after his successful [[Capture of Eeth Koth/Legends|capture of Eeth Koth]]. This droid was later informed by Grievous that the approaching Republic forces led by Jedi would be a two-pronged attack: one aimed at distracting him and the other aimed at rescuing [[Eeth Koth/Legends|Eeth Koth]]. The [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] General's predictions came true when [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] along with [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]] arrived covertly on [[Grievous's Recusant-class light destroyer/Legends|Grievous' Separatist destroyer]]. The tactical droid sprang an ambush which consisted of [[BX-series droid commando/Legends|BX-series droid commandos]] and admitted that Grievous's predictions had surprised it. This tactical droid also attempted to dissuade the Jedi from attacking by inducing electrical shocks in Eeth Koth and later claimed that the next tap of the button would kill the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] member. However, Skywalker used [[The Force/Legends|The Force]] to bring the tactical droid to him and severed its arm, preventing it from activating the button. As the battle raged, the tactical droid reclaimed its arm and chuckled at its success but lacked a limb to press the button, whereupon the Jedi terminated the droid's existence.

Droid [[TV-94B/Legends|TV-94B]] was stationed on Grievous' Command ship during his [[Battle of Kamino/Legends|assault]] on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]].<ref name="ARC Troopers">{{TCW|ARC Troopers (episode)}}</ref>

Another [[Unidentified T-series tactical droid (Malastare)|droid]] commanded the CIS forces during the [[Battle of Malastare/Legends|Battle of Malastare]], where he was destroyed by the Republic's [[Electro-proton bomb/Legends|Electro-proton bomb]].<ref name="TZB">{{TCW|The Zillo Beast}}</ref>

[[File:TacticalDroidBlaster-SW.png|thumb|right|250px|TX-20 armed with an E-5 blaster rifle]]
Another [[Hoom Garaf's T-series tactical droid|droid]] executed [[Chevin/Legends|Chevin]] [[Major/Legends|Major]] [[Hoom Garaf]] during the [[Third Battle of Aefao]]. However it's action started a chaotic firefight in Separatist rear guard, which later ensured a Republic victory.<ref name="TEGTW" />

A [[Unidentified T-series tactical droid (Plagen)|tactical droid]] won a victory at the [[First Battle of Plagen]]. Before the battle, the droid had assassinated [[Kerkoiden/Legends|Kerkoiden]] General [[Piar Nagelsa/Legends|Piar Nagelsa]] and discarded his battle plan.<ref name="TEGTW" />

By around [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="Death Sentence 1">[[Darth Maul — Death Sentence 1|''Darth Maul — Death Sentence'' 1]]</ref> the Confederacy, considering standard tactical droids to be easily outmaneuvered by the Republic, manufactured the [[Super tactical droid/Legends|super tactical droid]] to compensate for the tactical droid's weaknesses. [[Kalani/Legends|Kalani]] was one of the droids in the new super tactical droid line.<ref name="Encyclopedia: Kalani">{{SWE|characters|general-kalani|General Kalani}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Tactical-concept.jpg|thumb|left|200px|An early concept for the [[original trilogy]], which ultimately became the tactical droid]]
Tactical droids were introduced in the animated TV series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' to create competent enemy commanders that were simultaneously disposable. In part, this was meant to create a degree of variety in the TV series so that the same enemies would not be defeated continuously.<ref name="Innocents of Ryloth Ep Guide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode020.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Innocents of Ryloth}}</ref>

The word "tactical" is written along the side of the head of at least [[TJ-55/Legends|one tactical droid]] in [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]].<ref name="The Hidden Enemy Ep Guide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode016.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: The Hidden Enemy}}</ref>

Because the crew of ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' wanted different villains that were expendable, tactical droids were given different paint schemes and voices. Among those who have voiced tactical droids are [[James Arnold Taylor]], [[Matthew Wood]], [[Ashley Eckstein]], [[Phil LaMarr]], [[Corey Burton]], [[Gary Scheppke]] and [[Matt Lanter]].
